David Crowley

Democratic candidate for Governor / Lieutenant Governor, Wisconsin · Open seat

Milwaukee County Executive

David Crowley is the Milwaukee County Executive and the Democratic nominee for governor of Wisconsin in the open-seat race to succeed Gov. Tony Evers, who is not running again. He launched his campaign on Sept. 9, 2025, briefly suspended it in summer 2026, re-entered after Gov. Evers endorsed him, and narrowly defeated state Rep. Francesca Hong in the Aug. 11, 2026 Democratic primary. He faces Republican U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany on Nov. 3, 2026.

Where Crowley stands

School vouchers
Says he would not end the Milwaukee voucher program and would keep the statewide program. He argues the statewide program subsidizes families who could already afford private school.
Transportation funding
Open to new transportation user fees and to tolling to pay for transportation projects. Opposes indexing the gas tax to inflation.
Data center tax breaks
Says he would sign Republican-proposed legislation to repeal the state sales tax exemption for data centers, which reverses his earlier position.
Local government funding / shared revenue
Cites his work to pass 2023 Act 12, the shared revenue law. Says the state should increase shared revenue so local EMS and fire departments are funded.
Climate and environment
Says climate change is real. Wants the state's 2050 climate action plan to be enforceable and accountable, and supports building infrastructure that better withstands flooding.
Tribal relations
Says he would continue building government-to-government relationships with Wisconsin's Native nations.
Cost of living, health care, housing and schools
At his campaign launch, said he would focus on lowering costs for families, affordable health care and housing, and fully funding public schools.
